title: Let All Our Tongues Be One
description: Let All Our Tongues Be One in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 10 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 9, headed “The Spirit, the water, and the blood, John 5. 6”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let all our tongues be one To praise our God on high, Who from his bo-som sent his Son To fetch us stran-gers nigh.

lines: Let all our tongues be one
To praise our God on high,
Who from his bosom sent his Son
It cost him cries and tears
To bring us near to God;
Great was our debt, and he appears
On the cold ground his life was spilt,
Look up, my soul, to him
And humbly view the living stream
And when the Spirit speaks the same
Here I believe he dy'd for me,
Lord, cleanse my soul from sin,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
